why.text: Hot summers and cold winters on potassium-rich red soils give fresh, aromatic wines. Whites from Malvar and Torrontés stand out.

styles.text: Light, fresh whites and rosados (Torrontés), plus moderately tannic reds: young, aged or carbonic-maceration.

climate.text: From 40 °C in summer to -8 °C in winter, with about 500 mm of rain a year.

soil.text: Deep red silty-clay soil with gravel; alkaline, low in organic matter and phosphorus, rich in potassium.

tastes.text: Whites: yellow, light, perfumed and pleasantly acidic; Torrontés intensely aromatic. Rosés: pink, red fruit and flowers, fresh. Reds: cherry, garnet or ruby, fruity, moderately tannic; aged ones tile-coloured, toasty, spiced.

styles.name: Maceración carbónica
styles.text: Silky, very tannic, with a persistent fruity finish.

styles.name: Fermentado en barrica
styles.text: White or rosé; fruit and floral aromas balanced with barrel.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva y Gran Reserva
styles.text: Tile tones; oak and stewed fruit, toast, spice; fleshy, persistent.

why.text: Low yields (about 3,000 kg/ha) give deeply coloured reds with ripe fruit. The sierra zones add minerality, while the chalky south-east adds ripeness.

styles.text: Fruity whites, rosados from dry to sweet, warm tannic reds, and quality sparkling wines.

soil.text: Chalky ground in the south-east; the sierra zones give mineral, scrubland notes.

tastes.text: Whites: pale straw, fruity; gold when aged. Rosés: strawberry, raspberry or salmon pink; red fruit, fresh. Reds: violet to cherry, ruby to tile when aged; fruity, tannic, warm, persistent; oak, spice and dried fruit with age.

styles.name: Vino espumoso de calidad
styles.text: Fine, abundant, lasting bubbles; fruity aromas; fresh and sharp.

styles.name: Crianza y Reserva
styles.text: White wines age to deep golden or old gold.

why.text: An extreme continental climate meets sandy, acidic soil poor in lime. The wines are warm and full-bodied, with high alcohol.

styles.text: Dry to sweet whites and rosados, young and oak-aged reds, and sparkling wines.

climate.text: Extreme continental: long cold winters, hot summers and very little rain.

soil.text: Sandy, acidic soil with very little lime.

tastes.text: Whites: pale straw, fruity with floral touches; oak versions pastry and toast. Rosés: strawberry pink, fresh. Reds: cherry to dark garnet; blackberry, redcurrant, flowers; fleshy, warm, well-integrated tannins; long, intense finish.

styles.name: Roble
styles.text: White with pastry notes such as cream and a toasty base.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva y Gran Reserva
styles.text: Cherry to ruby-tile; structured, oak notes, long and intense.

styles.name: Vino espumoso
styles.text: Fine, lasting bubbles; fruity aromas; reservas more intense.

why.text: Altitude and potassium-rich soils, with low-density bush vines, give balanced grapes. The wines are acidic and made to last in bottle.

styles.text: Reds, young whites and barrel-fermented or aged whites, rosados, and quality sparkling wines.

soil.text: Fine-textured, deep, tending to chalky; clay-loam to sandy-loam; rich in potassium.

altitude.text: 500 to 800 m in the west half; 600 to 1,200 m in the east.

tastes.text: Reds: deep colour, intense fruity and floral aromas; powerful, full-bodied, harmonious. Whites: pale yellow, fruity and fresh; barrel-fermented straw to golden, toasty. Rosés: strawberry or raspberry pink, fruity.

styles.name: Blanco fermentado en barrica
styles.text: Straw to golden; toasty barrel notes, soft texture, fruity finish.

styles.name: Espumoso de calidad
styles.text: Pale, small persistent bubbles; fruity aroma; fresh and balanced.

why.text: Between two river valleys, summers are hot and sunny with almost no rain. On calcareous clay soils, Bobal gives aromatic, deeply coloured wines.

styles.text: Dry to sweet whites and rosados; young, oak-aged and carbonic-maceration reds; sparkling white and rosé.

climate.text: High temperatures, almost no rain from May to September, and many hours of sun.

soil.text: Clay soils with a limestone base, from the sediments of two rivers.

tastes.text: Whites: very pale yellow with green glints, fruity. Rosés: strawberry, raspberry, bright, fresh, harmonious. Reds: cherry to ruby with violet; wild red fruit, long. Aged reds: garnet to tile; vanilla, toast, spice, jam.

styles.name: Fermentado en barrica
styles.text: Primary fruit and floral aromas in balance with the barrel.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva y Gran Reserva
styles.text: Garnet or ruby with tile tones; vanilla, toast; medium-high to high tannin.

styles.name: Vino espumoso
styles.text: White or rosé; small persistent bubbles; fruity, fresh and balanced.

why.text: The Júcar canyon brings more rain than the surrounding flatland. Lake-deposit soils give soft, balanced wines with good acidity.

styles.text: Dry and sweet whites and rosados; young, traditional, crianza and reserva reds.

climate.text: The Júcar canyon causes more rain than the surrounding area. The document gives no figures.

soil.text: Lake deposits: silty sands, salty clays, gravel and rounded dolomitic limestone cemented by clay.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow, fruity, soft. Rosés: pink, moderate body. Young reds: cherry-red, red fruit, powerful, round. Aged reds: ruby to tile; floral, spice, balsamic, toast; velvety, long; vanilla, pepper and cocoa after wood.

styles.name: Tradición
styles.text: Red and purple tones; intense, frank aromas; long, intense finish.

styles.name: Crianza y Reserva
styles.text: Ruby to cherry with tile tones; ripe red fruit; potent after wood.

why.text: Dry, chalky plains get 3,000 hours of sun and 300 to 350 mm of rain. Wines are colourful and aromatic, balanced by low yields.

styles.text: Whites and rosados, young or traditional; oak and aged reds; naturally sweet wine; semi-sparkling and sparkling wines.

climate.text: Extreme continental: high temperatures, 300 to 350 mm of rain a year and about 3,000 hours of sun.

soil.text: Miocene limestone, marl and sand, brown to red-brown; chalky soils give full-bodied reds.

tastes.text: Whites: yellow short of gold, fruity, slightly acidic; oaked ones toasty with vanilla. Rosés: pale pink to red, fruity. Reds: violet to garnet, fruity, tannic; oaked ones vanilla; aged ones tile-edged, soft.

styles.name: Tradicional Naturalmente Dulce
styles.text: White; glyceric, raisins and stone fruit, velvety, long finish.

styles.name: Roble
styles.text: Red garnet to ruby; vanilla; persistent and balanced.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva y Gran Reserva
styles.text: White or red; vanilla and toast; reds from cherry to tile.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: White, rosé or red; fruity, broad and balanced, carbonic gas noticeable.

why.text: Almansa is a high plateau with an extreme continental climate and limestone-rich soil. Yields of 4,500 kg/ha concentrate colour and tannin in the wines.

styles.text: Young and barrel-aged whites, rosados and reds, dry to sweet; reds also crianza, reserva and gran reserva.

climate.text: Extreme continental: very cold dry winters, very hot summers, under 250 mm of rain a year on average, mostly spring and late summer.

soil.text: Rich in limestone, from thin stony patches to deeper sandy ones.

altitude.text: Plateau from 400 m at Fuente la Higuera to 700 m at Almansa.

tastes.text: Whites: light, sustained yellow, mildly aromatic. Rosés: strawberry to raspberry pink, fruity. Reds: violet, deep colour, fleshy, lightly tannic; oaked ones toasty. Aged reds: cherry or garnet, tile tones, fruit and spice.

styles.name: Roble
styles.text: Red; medium persistence with toasty touches.

styles.name: Fermentado en barrica
styles.text: White; straw to gold; primary and toasty aromas; soft, with fruity finish.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva y Gran Reserva
styles.text: Red; fruit and oak well joined, or spice; medium tannin.

why.text: A Mediterranean climate with low rain in key months cuts disease. Reds are rich in tannin and colour, while whites are fruity with medium-high acidity.

styles.text: Fruity whites, rosados and reds rich in tannin and colour; whites and reds also aged (crianza, reserva).

climate.text: Mediterranean, with low rainfall in the decisive months of the growing season, so little fungal disease.

tastes.text: Whites: greenish to straw, white, yellow, citrus or exotic fruit. Rosés: pink to red; red or black fruit. Reds: violet tones, medium colour; red, black or raisined fruit. Aged wines: wood and toast.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva y Gran Reserva
styles.text: Wood and toast aromas and flavours; whites soft to golden yellow.

why.text: Dark volcanic-zone soils warm up early. Dry air and about 400 mm of rain let vines ripen with little disease.

styles.text: Dry to sweet whites, rosados and reds, from young to gran reserva; sparkling white and rosé; some over-ripe red.

climate.text: Mean 15.6 °C, no more than about 400 mm of rain, 52% humidity, over 2,800 sun hours; disease risk almost nil.

soil.text: Dark clay-loam soils, often stony; low in calcium, high in potassium; volcanic rock.

altitude.text: Gentle hills at 700 to 900 m, small plains at 630 to 650 m.

tastes.text: Whites: yellow range; white and tropical fruit, white flowers, citrus. Rosés: violet-pink to salmon; red and black fruit. Reds: red range without orange; red and black fruit, spice, toasty oak; medium acidity and tannin.

styles.name: Clásico
styles.text: Bright; medium or high colour; floral, fruity, spiced aromas.

styles.name: Roble
styles.text: Red fruit, spice and at least one of nut, toast, balsamic, mineral.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva y Gran Reserva
styles.text: Reds reach ochre or brown; stewed fruit, nuts, toast, balsamic.

why.text: A dry continental climate and chalky, humus-poor soil stress the vines. Low yields give well-structured, complex reds.

styles.text: Whites, rosados, reds including a traditional style, and sparkling wine.

climate.text: Dry continental; high summer temperatures ease off late, slowing the end of ripening and keeping aromas.

soil.text: Chalky, poor in organic matter, pH 7.5 to 8.5, easy for roots to penetrate; reflects sunlight, stores heat.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow, golden after barrel; fine, clean, discreetly fruity. Rosés: pink with red and violet; fresh, fruity. Reds: picota to violet cherry or ruby; subtle aroma growing with time; soft, warm, long finish.

styles.name: Tinto Tradicional
styles.text: Violet to garnet red; frank, fruity, medium aromatic intensity.

styles.name: Vino espumoso
styles.text: Pale or golden; fine, persistent bubbles; clean, fruity aromas.
